title: Cover every entry point
body: Burglars favour front doors, back doors and ground-floor windows. Place cameras so each of these is in view, and mount them high enough to be out of easy reach.

title: Check your night vision
body: Test your cameras after dark at least once. Dirty lenses, spider webs and bright security lights can wash out the picture just when you need it.

title: Sensors beat guesswork
body: A door or window contact sensor alerts your phone the moment something opens, even when nobody is looking at the camera feed.

title: Mind the pets
body: If you have pets, choose pet-immune motion sensors or place them so animals are not triggering false alarms every night.

title: Retire the hidden spare key
body: The flowerpot is the first place a thief looks. A keypad smart lock lets you issue and cancel PIN codes for family, helpers and visitors.

title: Review your access log
body: Smart locks record who came and went. A quick weekly look at the log shows unexpected entries early.

title: Make the house look lived-in
body: Use timers on lights, ask a neighbour to collect post and avoid announcing holidays on social media.

title: Know your neighbours
body: A neighbourhood WhatsApp group with active neighbours is one of the cheapest and most effective security upgrades.
